review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος Θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ σὺν τοῖς ἁγίοις πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἀχαΐᾳ·
1:1.targetText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother,  To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:

groups.note: The article ὁ is used as a possessive and rendered our.
ἐν ὅλῃ ("in the whole of") is rendered throughout.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves τῇ οὔσῃ ("which is") untranslated.
BSB leaves τοῖς οὖσιν ("who are") untranslated.

1:2.sourceText: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:2.targetText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

1:3.sourceText: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ Θεὸς καὶ Πατὴρ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ Πατὴρ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν καὶ Θεὸς πάσης παρακλήσεως,
1:3.targetText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in this Greek nominal blessing; no Greek verb is written.

1:4.sourceText: ὁ παρακαλῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν, εἰς τὸ δύνασθαι ἡμᾶς παρακαλεῖν τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως ἧς παρακαλούμεθα αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ Θεοῦ.
1:4.targetText: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.

groups.note: The article with the participle παρακαλῶν ("comforting") is rendered who comforts.
εἰς τό with the infinitive is rendered so that.
παρακαλούμεθα ("we are comforted") is rendered with the comfort we have received.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the relative ἧς ("with which") untranslated.

1:5.sourceText: ὅτι καθὼς περισσεύει τὰ παθήματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς, οὕτως διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ περισσεύει καὶ ἡ παράκλησις ἡμῶν.
1:5.targetText: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:6.sourceText: εἴτε δὲ θλιβόμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως καὶ σωτηρίας· εἴτε παρακαλούμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως τῆς ἐνεργουμένης ἐν ὑπομονῇ τῶν αὐτῶν παθημάτων ὧν καὶ ἡμεῖς πάσχομεν.
1:6.targetText: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.

groups.note: The article with the participle ἐνεργουμένης ("being at work") is rendered which accomplishes.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB makes ἐν ὑπομονῇ ("in endurance") the object of accomplishes, so ἐν has no English word.
BSB leaves the relative ὧν ("which") untranslated.
BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek phrase has no verb.
English supplies a subject and copula; the Greek phrase has no verb.

1:7.sourceText: καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν βεβαία ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν, εἰδότες ὅτι ὡς κοινωνοί ἐστε τῶν παθημάτων, οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως.
1:7.targetText: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.

groups.note: The participle εἰδότες ("knowing") is rendered because … know.
κοινωνοί ἐστε ("you are sharers") is rendered you share and is understood again in the second clause.
The article τῶν is used as a possessive and rendered our.
The article τῆς is used as a possessive and rendered our.

1:8.sourceText: Οὐ γὰρ θέλομεν ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν τῆς γενομένης ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ἐβαρήθημεν, ὥστε ἐξαπορηθῆναι ἡμᾶς καὶ τοῦ ζῆν·
1:8.targetText: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.

groups.note: The possessive ἡμῶν ("our") is rendered as the subject we.
The article with the participle γενομένης ("that came") is rendered encountered.
καθ’ ὑπερβολήν ("beyond measure") is rendered far.
The articular infinitive τοῦ ζῆν ("of living") is rendered of life.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence, so ὅτι ("that") has no English word.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB adds that Asia was a Roman province.
English supplies whose ability is meant.
English supplies what the ability was for.

1:9.sourceText: ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς τὸ ἀπόκριμα τοῦ θανάτου ἐσχήκαμεν, ἵνα μὴ πεποιθότες ὦμεν ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τῷ Θεῷ τῷ ἐγείροντι τοὺς νεκρούς·
1:9.targetText: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.

groups.note: ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ("in ourselves") is rendered felt.
ἐσχήκαμεν ("we have had") is rendered we were under.
The article with the participle ἐγείροντι ("raising") is rendered who raises.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

1:10.sourceText: ὃς ἐκ τηλικούτου θανάτου ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς καὶ ῥύσεται, εἰς ὃν ἠλπίκαμεν ὅτι καὶ ἔτι ῥύσεται,
1:10.targetText: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,

groups.note: The relative ὅς ("who") is rendered He.
θανάτου ("death") is rendered deadly peril.
One ἡμᾶς is the object of all three deliver verbs; BSB repeats us.
καὶ ἔτι ("even still") is rendered yet again.

1:11.sourceText: συνυπουργούντων καὶ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῇ δεήσει, ἵνα ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων τὸ εἰς ἡμᾶς χάρισμα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστηθῇ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν.
1:11.targetText: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers.

groups.note: The genitive absolute συνυπουργούντων ("joining in helping") is rendered as … help.
ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ("on our behalf") is rendered as the object of help.
The article τῇ is used as a possessive and rendered your.
ἵνα ("so that") is rendered Then, starting a new sentence.
ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων ("from many faces") is rendered many.
εἰς ἡμᾶς ("toward us") is rendered shown us.
διά ("through") is rendered in answer to.
The second πολλῶν ("many") is rendered their, referring back to the many.
BSB makes the passive εὐχαριστηθῇ ("may be thanked for") active.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves καί ("also") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies what the many did; the Greek has no word for prayer here.

1:12.sourceText: Ἡ γὰρ καύχησις ἡμῶν αὕτη ἐστίν, τὸ μαρτύριον τῆς συνειδήσεως ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐν ἁγιότητι καὶ εἰλικρινίᾳ τοῦ Θεοῦ, οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ σαρκικῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν χάριτι Θεοῦ, ἀνεστράφημεν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, περισσοτέρως δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.
1:12.targetText: And this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God—not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.

groups.note: γάρ ("for") is rendered And.
μαρτύριον ("testimony") is rendered as the verb testifies.
Same word, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
The genitive τοῦ Θεοῦ ("of God") is rendered from God.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause with a copula; the Greek phrase has no verb.

1:13.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἄλλα γράφομεν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἢ ἃ ἀναγινώσκετε ἢ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκετε, ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι ἕως τέλους ἐπιγνώσεσθε,
1:13.targetText: For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely,

groups.note: ἄλλα … ἀλλ’ ἤ ("other things … than") is rendered anything … beyond.
ἀναγινώσκετε ("you read") is rendered your ability to read.
ἤ ("or") is rendered and.
ἕως τέλους ("to the end") is rendered completely.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts ἃ ἀναγινώσκετε ("what you read") as your ability to read, so the relative ἅ has no English word.
BSB leaves καί ("even") untranslated.

1:14.sourceText: καθὼς καὶ ἐπέγνωτε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ μέρους, ὅτι καύχημα ὑμῶν ἐσμεν καθάπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ.
1:14.targetText: as you have already understood us in part, so that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.

groups.note: ὅτι ("that") is rendered so that.
καύχημα ἐσμεν ("we are a boast") is recast as boast of us, and BSB repeats boast of in the comparison.
ὑμῶν ("your") becomes the subject you of boast.
ὑμεῖς ("you"), the subject in Greek, becomes the ones boasted of.
ἡμῶν ("ours") becomes the subject we of boast.

1:15.sourceText: Καὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πεποιθήσει ἐβουλόμην πρότερον πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν ἵνα δευτέραν χάριν σχῆτε,
